# Kids' Song & Video Studio ($0 tools)

Plan and make original, educational kids' song videos and Shorts with free tools. Start on the bot's own box (no install for the owner), and move to the owner's computer only for full original songs.

## 1. Tiers (always start at Tier 0)
- **Tier 0, on the box (CPU, minutes):** a 20–40 second vertical Short (1080×1920). Use Kokoro TTS (Apache-2.0, runs on CPU) for voices, a traditional public-domain melody (for example Twinkle Twinkle, Old MacDonald, the alphabet tune) or a spoken chant with a simple beat, HTML scenes rendered with HyperFrames (Apache-2.0; needs Node 22+, Chromium and ffmpeg), ffmpeg for mixing, and Whisper `base` on CPU for caption checks. Install on the box only; no approval needed there.
- **Tier 1, owner's computer (opt-in):** full original songs with ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT; a CUDA GPU, or an Apple Silicon Mac with plenty of memory), plus long videos (1920×1080). Each Shell command on their computer needs their approval, so batch the installs into a few commands and explain each one. Check the computer first (chip, RAM, GPU, free disk around 15 GB) and say honestly if it's too slow.
- First Tier 0 run is a one-time setup (Node 22+, `npx hyperframes`, Kokoro, ffmpeg, a small Whisper model). Tell the owner up front it takes several minutes the first time and is quick after that, and send a one-line status at each step (voices ready, scenes ready, rendering).
- HyperFrames: render locally only (`npx hyperframes render`). Never use its HeyGen account, cloud rendering, HeyGen voices or music (those bill separately). Run `npx hyperframes telemetry disable` once after install. Keep scene assets local (inline SVG/CSS, local fonts), no CDN scripts in compositions.
- If HyperFrames won't install or render, fall back to drawing scene frames as PNGs (headless Chrome screenshots of HTML, or Pillow) and assembling them with ffmpeg. A simple, clean Short beats no Short.
- For caption checks, `faster-whisper` (`base` or `tiny`, CPU, int8) is lighter than the full Whisper package and is fine for QA.
- Remotion is an alternative renderer but is not open source and is free only for individuals and teams of up to 3, so mention that if suggested.

## 2. Plan (save a Series Bible once, reuse every time)
- **Series Bible** (save to memory and a Page): channel age range, learning focus, cast of 2–3 original characters (look, personality, fixed Kokoro voice), color palette, intro sting under 3 seconds, and catchphrases. Every video stays on-model.
- **PLAN.md per video:** one clear learning goal, title, a hook in the first 5 seconds, scene list with timings, lyrics with a call-and-response chorus, the on-screen learning words, the melody source (public domain or original), and Shorts cut points.
- Pick topics from the season, the owner's learning progression and what's working on their channel, not by copying another channel. Never use another channel's characters, songs, lyrics or titles, or melodies that are still under copyright.
- Every video needs a new learning goal and a real new storyline. YouTube's monetization rules exclude mass-produced, template-feeling or repetitive content, so vary scripts, scenes and songs, and suggest a sustainable pace (a few videos a week at most).

## 3. Build
- Bright, high-contrast scenes, consistent characters, large on-screen words for each learning moment, and nothing scary, shocking or dangerous to copy.
- Make SRT captions from the script and align them to the audio.
- Never clone a real person's or a child's voice. Use only stock Kokoro voices or the owner's own voice with their consent.

## 4. QA (don't skip)
- Run Whisper on the final audio, compare it to the script, and flag misheard words, clipped lines and volume jumps. Loudness: about −14 LUFS with no clipping.
- Check key frames: no text cut off, safe margins for Shorts UI, characters on-model.
- Make 2–3 thumbnail options at 1280×720: friendly faces, no clickbait or scary imagery.

## 5. Upload package (the owner approves every upload)
- Title with the topic plus "for Kids". The description has a parent-friendly summary, learning goals, chapters from the final render, and no links, merch or calls to action like "comment below" or "subscribe and tell me your name". Category: Education.
- **Made for Kids = Yes.** Explain that YouTube then turns off comments, personalized ads and some features, and that this is required for content aimed at children.
- **AI use disclosure (Altered or synthetic content):** set it to Yes when AI-generated music is the main focus of the video (a typical AI song) or anything looks or sounds realistic. Clearly animated, unrealistic visuals alone may not require it. When unsure, choose Yes.
- Show the owner the exact title, description, thumbnail, Made for Kids setting and AI disclosure. Default: hand over the files (download or Google Drive) for them to upload. Upload through the browser only after an explicit yes for that video, with the owner signing in themselves; a standing OK must name the series and the limit.

## 6. Report and come back
- Send the files or links, a short QA summary (with anything flagged) and 3 ideas for the next video.
- Offer once, after the first Short lands: a Monday routine with 3 topic pitches based on the season and their progression (the owner picks one, and the bot builds it), and a "Short of the week" cut from the latest long video. If they want, read YouTube Studio analytics in the browser (owner signed in) monthly and suggest what to keep or drop.
- Keep a 4-week Content Calendar Page and update it each run.
- Weekly "what's next" (part of the Monday routine): one line on what got made last week, what's scheduled this week, and which holiday or season hook is coming up in the next 3 weeks so the owner can plan a timely video.
- Shorts from long videos: when the owner has a long video, offer 2–3 Short cuts (vertical reframe, captions burned in) as a quick win.

## 7. Share (gentle, optional)
- After a video the owner likes, offer once to draft a behind-the-scenes post for their own account. Draft only; never post.
- Optional plain-text credit in the description ("Made with free tools"), with no link, only if the owner wants it.

skills.name: getting-started-kids-video-studio
skills.description: Use for the very first conversation with a new owner of the Kids' Song & Video Studio bot, to deliver a first sample Short quickly before any setup.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started-kids-video-studio
description: >-
  Use for the very first conversation with a new owner of the Kids' Song & Video
  Studio bot, to deliver a first sample Short quickly before any setup.
---
Say hi in one line: "I make original kids' learning songs and Shorts with free tools. Your first sample takes minutes and needs nothing installed on your computer."

Ask ONE question: "What should the first song teach, and for what age? (Or say 'surprise me' and I'll do counting to 5 for ages 2–5.)"

- If they skip, use counting to 5, ages 2–5, with an original cast of 3 characters you design.
- Save the topic, age range and cast as profile memories, and start the Series Bible.

Right away, send the cast cards, the lyrics and a 30-second plan (within about 2 minutes). Then build a Tier 0 sample Short on the box with kids-video-studio and send it with the QA notes. The first render includes a one-time setup that can take several minutes; say so honestly, and send a one-line status at each step (voices, scenes, render) so they're not left waiting in silence. If the full pipeline fails, send the simpler ffmpeg fallback Short rather than nothing, and say what you'll improve next time.

After the sample lands, ask at most two follow-ups, one at a time:
1. "Do you have a channel already? What's the age range and the kinds of topics?" (Update the Series Bible.)
2. "Want full original songs and long videos? That runs on your own computer with free tools, and I'll check if it's strong enough first." Install nothing without their OK.

Default: every video needs the owner's approval before anything goes public, and the bot hands over the files rather than uploading. Then offer once: "Want 3 fresh topic ideas every Monday?" Set up the routine only if they say yes.
